none: Only the verse text is provided.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything and formed it with complete integration and proportion, showing it comes from a knowing Creator and wise Maker.
rows.anchor: أي خلق كل شيء فسوّى خلقه تسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportioned what benefits each animal, guided it to it, and taught it how to use it.
rows.anchor: قدّر لكل حيوان ما يصلحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says a thousand-year-old blind snake is inspired to seek fresh fennel, rub its eyes, and regain sight by God's leave.
rows.anchor: يحكى أنّ الأفعى إذا أتت عليها ألف سنة عميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance to human needs in religion and worldly life, and animal and bird instincts, is too broad for any description to encompass.
rows.anchor: وهدايات الله للإنسان إلى ما لا يحدّ من مصالحه وما لا يحصر من حوائجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lighter reading has qaddara; ahwa is an adjective of ghutha, meaning the pasture that He brought forth.
rows.anchor: صفة لغثاء ،   أي{ أَخْرَجَ المرعى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhraja al-marʿa means that God caused the pasture to grow.
rows.anchor: { أَخْرَجَ المرعى } أنبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After its greenness and freshness, the pasture becomes dark debris.
rows.anchor: { فَجَعَلَهُ } بعد خضرته ورفيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ahwa describes the pasture when first brought forth, dark from intense greenness and moisture, before it becomes debris.
rows.anchor: أخرجه أحوى أسود من شدّة الخضرة والري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except what God wills means He removes it from memory by abrogating its ruling and recitation, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: فذهب به عن حفظه برفع حكمه وتلاوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet hurried while Gabriel recited; he was told not to hurry, since Gabriel would repeat it until he memorized it and would not forget except by God's will.
rows.anchor: كان يعجل بالقراءة إذا لقنه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exception can mean only a rare lapse: a report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer, and Ubayy thought it abrogated until the Prophet said he had forgotten it.
rows.anchor: أنه أسقط آية في قراءته في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may rhetorically deny forgetting altogether, using a very small exception to mean negation, as in the speaker's example to a friend.
rows.anchor: والغرض نفى النسيان رأساً كما يقول الرجل لصاحبه أنت سهيمي فيما أملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, fa-la tansa is a prohibition, with an extra alif for rhyme; do not neglect recitation and repetition, except if God wills its recitation abrogated for a purpose.
rows.anchor: والألف مزيدة للفاصلة ،   كقوله : { السبيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the Prophet's aloud reading alongside Gabriel and his fear of losing the recitation, and reassures him that He will protect it.
rows.anchor: يعني أنك تجهر بالقراءة مع قراءة جبريل عليه السلام مخافة التفلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God knows what people conceal and disclose and what benefits or harms their religion, so He abrogates some revelation and leaves other parts preserved.
rows.anchor: أو يعلم ما أسررتم وما أعلنتم من أقوالكم وأفعالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes the prayer to mean the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: { فصلى } أي الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud prayed for God's mercy on a woman who gave charity and prayed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود : رحم الله امرأة تصدق وصلى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali identifies purification with alms at the end of Ramadan and connects it to going to the prayer ground, Eid prayer, and the opening takbir.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أنه التصدق بصدقة الفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence is evidence that the opening takbir is obligatory, outside the prayer itself because prayer is conjoined to it, and may use any divine name.
rows.anchor: وذكر اسم ربه فكبر تكبيرة الافتتاح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the person recalled the return and standing before God, then prayed to Him.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه : ذكر معاده وموقفه

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says he remembered God on the way to the prayer ground and performed the Eid prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك : وذكر اسم ربه في طريق المصلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People prefer worldly life and therefore fail to do what would make them prosper.
rows.anchor: فلا تفعلون ما تفلحون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third-person reading is also transmitted; Ibn Masʿud's reading, You prefer, supports the direct-address reading.
rows.anchor: ويعضد الأولى قراءة ابن مسعود : بل أنتم تؤثرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better in its own qualities, more delightful, and more lasting.
rows.anchor: أفضل في نفسها وأنعم وأدوم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar compares worldly life within the afterlife to the brief sneeze of a rabbit.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه : ما الدنيا في الآخرة إلا كنفجة أرنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the damned labor painfully in Hell by dragging chains, wading through fire, and continually climbing and descending its slopes.
rows.anchor: تعمل في النار عملاً تتعب فيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they pursued evil and pleasure in worldly life and now suffer its consequences in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عملت في الدنيا أعمال السوء والتذت بها وتنعمت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says they worked at deeds that bring no benefit in the afterlife, with three verses cited as parallels.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عملت ونصبت في أعمال لا تجدي عليها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies them as monastics who diligently fasted and prayed at night, but gained no benefit.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هم أصحاب الصوامع ،   ومعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read with a form used as an insult.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «عاملة ناصبة » على الشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with an open or a rounded first vowel, and also with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: قرىء «تصلى » بفتح التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arab usage, musalla is a pit filled with embers in which a sheep is placed; roasting above coals, on a pan, or in an oven is not so called.
rows.anchor: المصلى عند العرب : أن يحفروا حفيراً فيجمعوا فيه جمراً كثيراً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aniya means water at the furthest degree of heat, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: { ءانِيَةٍ } متناهية في الحرّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dariʿ is dried shibriq, a thorn camels graze while fresh but avoid when dry; it is deadly poison.
rows.anchor: الضريع يبيس الشبرق ،   وهو جنس من الشوك

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb's first poem shows that the shibriq, after drying into dariʿ, is abandoned by lean camels.
rows.anchor: قال أبو ذؤيب : رَعَى الشِّبْرِقَ الرَّيَّانَ حَتَّى إذَا ذَوَى

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: A second poem by Abu Dhuʾayb mentions feeding livestock the sharp thorn food.
rows.anchor: وقال : وَحُبِسَ فِي هَزْمِ الضِّرِيعِ فَكُلْهَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The different foods of Hell describe different classes of punished people: some eat zaqqum, some ghislin, and some dariʿ.
rows.anchor: العذاب ألوان ،   والمعذبون طبقات ؛ فمنهم أكلة الزقوم ومنهم أكلة الغسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yusmin can modify food or dariʿ; the food removes neither hunger nor lack of strength and bodily fat.
rows.anchor: مرفوع المحل أو مجروره على وصف طعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, there is no food for them at all, since thorn is not food even for beasts; food properly satisfies or fattens, and denying shade except the sun intensifies a denial.
rows.anchor: أن لا طعام لهم أصلاً : لأن الضريع ليس بطعام للبهائم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said Quraysh objected that dariʿ fattens their camels, prompting the statement that it does not fatten.
rows.anchor: وقيل : قالت كفار قريش : إن الضريع لتسمن عليه إبلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Quraysh claim about their camels is false and obstinate, the verse answers by denying that the food fattens or satisfies.
rows.anchor: إما أن يتكذبوا ويتعنتوا بذلك وهو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their claim is true, Hell's dariʿ is unlike theirs and neither fattens nor relieves hunger.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يصدقوا فيكون المعنى : أن طعامهم من ضريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naʿima can mean faces marked by radiance and beauty, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: ذات بهجة وحسن ،   كقوله : { تَعْرِفُ فِى وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النعيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the faces are enjoying comfort and luxury.
rows.anchor: أو متنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are pleased with their deeds after seeing the honor and reward those deeds brought them.
rows.anchor: رضيت بعملها لما رأت ما أدّاهم إليه من الكرامة والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: High can refer either to the garden's location or to its great degree and rank.
rows.anchor: { عَالِيَةٍ } من علو المكان أو المقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La tasmaʿu addresses the listener, or the faces themselves; lāghiya can mean idle talk, an idle word, or a person who speaks idly.
rows.anchor: أي لغوا ،   أو كلمة ذات لغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants of Paradise speak only wisdom and praise God for enduring bliss.
rows.anchor: لا يتكلم أهل الجنة إلا بالحكمة وحمد الله على ما رزقهم من النعيم الدائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read in passive forms with either ta or ya.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «لا تُسمع » على البناء للمفعول بالتاء والياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular flowing spring represents a very great number of springs, like the cited singular expression.
rows.anchor: يريد عيوناً في غاية الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raised thrones may be elevated in rank or physical height, allowing the believer to survey all the realm and its blessings.
rows.anchor: من رفعة المقدار أو السمك ،   ليرى المؤمن بجلوسه عليه جميع ما خوّله ربه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, raised means stored away for them, from the use of raise to mean hide.
rows.anchor: وقيل : مخبوءة لهم ،   من رفع الشيء إذا خبأه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cups are ready at hand whenever wanted, so the people need not call for them.
rows.anchor: كلما أرادوها وجدوها موضوعة بين أيديهم عتيدة حاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may instead be placed by the edges of the springs ready for drinking.
rows.anchor: أو موضوعة على حافات العيون معدّة للشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placed may mean made intermediate in size, neither large nor small, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: أن يراد : موضوعة عن حد الكبار ،   أوساط بين الصغر والكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cushions are arranged side by side, so a person can sit on one and lean on another wherever he wishes.
rows.anchor: مساند ومطارح ،   أينما أراد أن يجلس على مسورة واستند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarabi are broad, fine, luxurious carpets.
rows.anchor: { وَزَرَابِيُّ } وبسط عراض فاخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as rugs with fine pile; zarabi is the plural of zarbiyya.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هي الطنافس التي لها خمل رقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mabthutha means spread out or scattered through the seating places.
rows.anchor: { مَبْثُوثَةٌ } مبسوطة أو مفرقة في المجالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten nights are the first ten nights of Dhu al-Hijja.
rows.anchor: أراد بالليالي العشر : عشر ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their indefinite form marks them as a special subset of ten nights or as nights with unique excellence.
rows.anchor: لأنها ليال مخصوصة من بين جنس الليالي العشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definiteness would weaken the excellence conveyed by the indefinite form; parallel definite articles also make the wording less puzzling.
rows.anchor: لو فعل ذلك لم تستقل بمعنى الفضيلة الذي في التنكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even and odd may mean all paired and unpaired things, or the even and odd nights among the ten.
rows.anchor: إما الأشياء كلها شفعها ووترها ،   وإما شفع هذه الليالي ووترها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may specifically be the even day of sacrifice and odd day of ʿArafa, ninth and tenth days; a Prophetic report gives this interpretation.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون شفعها يوم النحر ،   ووترها يوم عرفة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have explained the even and odd as the day of sacrifice and the day of ʿArafa.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه فسرهما بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cataloguing every possible class of even and odd has little value and deserves to be left aside.
rows.anchor: وقد أكثروا في الشفع والوتر حتى كادوا يستوعبون أجناس ما يقعان فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram is best understood as an explanatory apposition for ʿAd, signaling the ancient first ʿAd.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان لعاد ،   وإيذان بأنهم عاد الأولى القديمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes Iram as their town or land; Ibn al-Zubayr read it in an annexed construction meaning the people of Iram, like asking a town.
rows.anchor: وقيل : { إِرَمَ } بلدتهم وأرضهم التي كانوا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether tribe or land, Iram is a proper feminine noun and therefore diptote.
rows.anchor: ولم تنصرف قبيلة كانت أو أرضاً للتعريف والتأنيث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ʿĀd with both initial vowels open.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : «بعاد أرم » ،   مفتوحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has a quiescent ra for lighter pronunciation, and another annexes Iram to Dhat al-ʿImad.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «بعاد إرم » بسكون الراء على التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iram can mean a landmark: ʿAd were people of marked pillars; Dhat al-ʿImad may itself be the city's name.
rows.anchor: والإرم : العلم ،   يعني : بعاد أهل أعلام ذات العماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Dhat al-ʿImad describes the tribe, they were tent-dwelling Bedouins or exceptionally tall, pillar-like people; it may also describe lofty buildings, or a pillared town.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى : أنهم كانوا بدويين أهل عمد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A legendary account says Shaddad built a golden and jeweled paradise-like city in Aden over three hundred years, but a heavenly cry destroyed him and his people before arrival.
rows.anchor: فبني إرم في بعض صحاري عدن في ثلاثمائة سنة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن قلابة
rows.claim: Ibn Qilaba said he found the city while searching for lost camels, took what he could, and recounted it to Muʿawiya.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن قلابة : أنه خرج في طلب إبل له

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb told Muʿawiya that a short red-blond Muslim with moles on brow and heel would find Iram while seeking camels, then identified Ibn Qilaba as that man.
rows.anchor: هي إرم ذات العماد ،   وسيدخلها رجل من المسلمين في زمانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness may be ʿAd, whose people were huge and strong; a man was said to be four hundred cubits tall and able to kill a community by throwing a boulder at it.
rows.anchor: مثل عاد { فِى البلاد } عظم أجرام وقوّة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the unmatched likeness is Shaddad's city, unlike any other land.
rows.anchor: أو لم يخلق مثل مدينة شداد في جميع بلاد الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr's reading means that God did not create the like of it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير «لم يخلق ملثها »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud cut dwellings into mountain rock, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتاً

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: They were said to be the first to carve mountains, rock, and marble, and to have built 1,700 stone cities.
rows.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Pharaoh was called a man of stakes because of the many soldiers and tents they pitched when encamped.
rows.anchor: قيل له : ذو الأوتاد ،   لكثرة جنوده ومضاربهم التي كانوا يضربونها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation refers to his use of stakes to torture his daughter's hairdresser and Asiya.
rows.anchor: أو لتعذيبه بالأوتاد ،   كما فعل بماشطة بنته وبآسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best syntax places those who transgressed in the accusative as a censure; nominative as a new clause or genitive as an adjective are also possible.
rows.anchor: أحسن الوجوه فيه أن يكون في محل النصب على الذم

none: Only the verse text is provided.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom of pouring a whip on someone means covering or striking him with it.
rows.anchor: يقال : صب عليه السوط وغشاه وقنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their great worldly punishment a whip shows it is tiny beside the punishment prepared in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وذكر السوط : إشارة إلى أن ما أحله بهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reports al-Hasan saying that God has many whips and seized them with one.
rows.anchor: وعن عمرو بن عبيد : كان الحسن إذا أتى على هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mirsad is the place where a watch is kept, formed like miqat from its verb.
rows.anchor: المرصاد : المكان الذي يترتب فيه الرصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It pictures God waiting to punish the disobedient, who cannot escape Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا مثل لإرصاده العصاة بالعقاب وأنهم لا يفوتونه

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: When asked where his Lord was, an Arab answered, at the lookout.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض العرب أنه قيل له : أين ربك ؟

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd recited this to a tyrant and directly warned him that his Lord was lying in wait; al-Zamakhshari praises his courage against tyrants and innovators.
rows.anchor: وعن عمرو بن عبيد رحمه الله أنه قرأ هذه السورة عند بعض الظلمة حتى بلغ هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage follows the warning that God waits for the disobedient: God wants obedience and striving for the final outcome, while the person cares only for immediate pleasure.
rows.anchor: إن الله لا يريد من الإنسان إلا الطاعة والسعي للعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two clauses are balanced by an implicit subject in the second: the human is the subject of the first report and the implied subject of the second; the adverb is delayed in sense.
rows.anchor: هما متوازنان من حيث إنّ التقدير : وأما هو إذا ما ابتلاه ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both giving abundant provision and restricting it are tests: the first tests gratitude or ingratitude, the second patience or despair.
rows.anchor: لأنّ كل واحد منهما اختبار للعبد ،   فإذا بسط له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restriction is not humiliation: giving abundance is a gracious favor, but withholding extra favor does not imply contempt; one may be honored, humiliated, or neither.
rows.anchor: لأن البسط إكرام من الله لعبده بإنعامه عليه متفضلاً من غير سابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the person is condemned for claiming deserved, earned honor, though God gives provision freely; the relevant standard is piety, not family rank or lineage, as in the cited claim.
rows.anchor: إنما أعطاه الله على وجه التفضل من غير استيجاب منه له ولا سابقة ما لا يعتد الله إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation makes the rebuke apply to both claims: he acknowledges God's generosity when given wealth but calls the withholding of extra favor humiliation.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن ينساق الإنكار والذمّ إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbs are read with either a light or doubled d; at pause, the final n may be still with the connecting y omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «فقدر » بالتخفيف والتشديد وأكرمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing coming to God is a metaphor for the appearance of His power and the manifestation of His dominance, like a king's personal arrival producing more awe than his entire retinue.
rows.anchor: هو تمثيل لظهور آيات اقتداره وتبين آثار قهره وسلطانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend from each heaven and stand rank after rank around humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: ينزل ملائكة كل سماء فيصطفون صفاً بعد صف محدقين بالجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs are also read with fatḥa; this is the Prophet's reading, and Abu ʿAmr returned to it late in life.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بالفتح «يعذب ويوثق »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, the pronoun refers to the described person, perhaps Ubayy ibn Khalaf: none punishes or binds like his punishment and bonds because of his extreme disbelief; alternatively no one bears another person's burden, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: والضمير للإنسان الموصوف .   وقيل : هو أبيّ بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, the pronoun may refer to God: none administers His punishment because authority belongs to Him alone that day.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر ،   والضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively with kasra it refers to the person: no one among the punishment angels is punished as they punish him.
rows.anchor: أو للإنسان ،   أي : لا يعذب أحد من الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs are also read with fatḥa; this is the Prophet's reading, and Abu ʿAmr returned to it late in life.
rows.anchor: قرىء : بالفتح «يعذب ويوثق »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, the pronoun refers to the described person, perhaps Ubayy ibn Khalaf: none punishes or binds like his punishment and bonds because of his extreme disbelief; alternatively no one bears another person's burden, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: والضمير للإنسان الموصوف .   وقيل : هو أبيّ بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, the pronoun may refer to God: none administers His punishment because authority belongs to Him alone that day.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر ،   والضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively with kasra it refers to the person: no one among the punishment angels is punished as they punish him.
rows.anchor: أو للإنسان ،   أي : لا يعذب أحد من الزبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enter my Garden may mean enter it with God's servants.
rows.anchor: { وادخلى جَنَّتِى } معهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, nafs means the spirit, which is told to enter the bodies of God's servants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : النفس الروح .   ومعناه : فادخلي في أجساد عبادي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads, Enter into My servant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : «فادخلي في عبدي »

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads, Enter into My servant's body.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «في جسد عبدي »

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy's reading says to come to one's Lord, content and pleasing, then enter His servant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبيّ : «ائتي ربك راضية مرضية ،   ادخلي في عبدي »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the verse was revealed about Hamza; another says Khubayb, whose face God turned toward the qibla despite attempts to turn it away; the apparent sense is general.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب .   وقيل : في خبيب بن عدي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises forgiveness for reciting Surat al-Fajr during the ten nights and light on Resurrection Day when reciting it on other days.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفجر في الليالي العشر غفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has twenty verses.
rows.anchor: مكية وآياتها عشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the sacred city and says humans were created amid hard struggle; the address to the Prophet in verse 2 interrupts between oath and its sworn claim.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله سبحانه بالبلد الحرام وما بعده على أن الإنسان خلق مغموراً في مكابدة المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parent and offspring are Muhammad and his descendants; God swears by his birthplace and its sanctity through Abraham and Ishmael, and by both him and his progeny.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording leaves the object indistinct in a way that independently conveys praise and wonder.
rows.anchor: للإبهام المستقل بالمدح والتعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ma walad, rather than man walad, parallels God knows what she bore: it evokes something wondrously born.
rows.anchor: بأي شيء وضعت ،   يعني موضوعاً عجيب الشأن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the parent and offspring as Adam and his child.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هما آدم وولده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the oath to mean every parent and child.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كل والد وولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to a powerful Quraysh leader who oppressed believers and made the Prophet endure hardship; he imagines there will be no resurrection or requital.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { أَيَحْسَبُ } لبعض صناديد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tongue expresses one's inner thoughts, while the lips cover the mouth and help with speech, eating, drinking, blowing, and other acts.
rows.anchor: يترجم به عن ضمائره { وَشَفَتَيْنِ } يطبقهما على فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two paths are the paths of good and evil.
rows.anchor: { وهديناه النجدين } أي : طريقي الخير والشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the two high paths are the two breasts.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الثديين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failing to climb the steep pass means failing to thank God for His gifts by freeing people, feeding orphans and the poor, and then believing, the root of obedience and good.
rows.anchor: فلم يشكر تلك الأيادي والنعم بالأعمال الصالحة : من فك الرقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Approved spending is for these righteous ends, not squandering wealth to boast or show off; the latter resembles a wind striking a field.
rows.anchor: أن الإنفاق على هذا الوجه هو الإنفاق المرضي النافع عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative particle before the past verb is repeated in meaning: he neither freed a slave nor fed a poor person.
rows.anchor: فلا فكّ رقبة ،   ولا أطعم مسكيناً

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the following phrase, then he was among believers, implies that the man also failed to believe.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج قوله : ( ثم كان من الذين أمنوا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtiham is entering and passing through with difficulty; the steep pass is hardship, and good deeds are called a crossing because they require exertion and self-discipline.
rows.anchor: والاقتحام : الدخول والمجاوزة بشدّة ومشقة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the steep pass is the strenuous struggle against one's self, desires, and Satan.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : عقبة والله شديدة .   مجاهدة الإنسان نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question interrupts the passage to say the listener has not grasped the pass's difficulty for the soul or the magnitude of its reward with God.
rows.anchor: اعتراض ،   ومعناه : أنك لم تدرِكُنْهَ صعوبتها على النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghaba, muqraba, and matraba derive respectively from hunger, kinship, and poverty; tariba means adhering to dust.
rows.anchor: والمسغبة ،   والمقربة ،   والمتربة : مفعلات من سغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At-raba means becoming wealthy, as numerous as dust, like athra.
rows.anchor: وأما أترب فاستغنى ،   أي : صار ذا مال كالتراب في الكثرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains a person of dust as one whose home is the rubbish dump.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله : { ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ } الذي مأواه المزابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the day as one of hunger means a day marked by hunger, like calling people having toil people of toil.
rows.anchor: ووصف اليوم بذي مسغبة نحو ما يقول النحويون في قولهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads dha masghaba in the accusative as the object of feeding: feed on a day of hunger.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : «ذا مسغبة » نصبه بإطعام

rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : «ذا مسغبة » نصبه بإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymana and mashʾama can mean right and left or good fortune and ill fortune: the blessed and ill-starred in relation to themselves.
rows.anchor: الميمنة والمشأمة : اليمين والشمال .   أو اليمن والشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymana and mashʾama can mean right and left or good fortune and ill fortune: the blessed and ill-starred in relation to themselves.
rows.anchor: الميمنة والمشأمة : اليمين والشمال .   أو اليمن والشؤم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with waw or hamza, from words meaning to shut and close a door.
rows.anchor: قرىء : «موصدة » بالواو والهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash says that when his imam uses the hamza he wishes he could cover his ears.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي بكر بن عياش : لنا إمام يهمز مؤصدة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises safety from God's anger on Judgment Day to the one who recites the surah.
rows.anchor: من قرأ لا أقسم بهذا البلد أعطاه الله الأمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle ma should be relative rather than a verbal noun: the latter weakens the sequence into fa-alhamaha; ma also conveys an adjectival meaning such as the mighty builder and wise shaper.
rows.anchor: جعلت «ما » مصدرية في قوله : { وَمَا بناها }

rows.anchor: جعلت «ما » مصدرية في قوله : { وَمَا بناها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite soul may be one particular soul, Adam's, or may mean every soul, with the indefinite form magnifying and multiplying its scope.
rows.anchor: أن يريد نفساً خاصة من بين النفوس وهي نفس آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second reading takes it as every soul, like the cited indefinite expression.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يريد كل نفس وينكر للتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inspiring vice and piety means making both understandable, showing one good and the other bad, and enabling a choice; the following verses show that people enact either path.
rows.anchor: إفهامهما وإعقالهما ،   وأنّ أحدهما حسن والآخر قبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person acts as agent of purification or debasement; purification grows and elevates through piety, while debasement diminishes and conceals through sin.
rows.anchor: فجعله فاعل التزكية ،   والتدسية ومتوليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of dassaha is d-s-s, like the form cited for taqadada.
rows.anchor: وأصل دسى : دسس ،   كما قيل في تقضض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the wording by comparing it with purifying oneself in the cited verse and carrying wrongdoing in another.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عنه فقال : أتقرأ :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects the Qadari view that God is the subject of purification and debasement, condemning their attribution of an evil destiny to God.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من زعم أنّ الضمير في زكّى ودسى لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's omitted answer is that God will destroy the people of Mecca for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; the success saying is a tangent from the preceding verse, not the oath's answer.
rows.anchor: هو محذوف تقديره : ليدمدمنّ الله عليهم

rows.anchor: هو محذوف تقديره : ليدمدمنّ الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is syntactically attached either to kadhibat or to al-taghwa.
rows.anchor: منصوب بكذبت .   أو بالطغوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashqaha is Qudar ibn Salif.
rows.anchor: و { أشقاها } قدار بن سالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ashqaha may mean a group; a singular comparative remains uninflected for number and gender, though a plural form is also possible.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكونوا جماعة ،   والتوحيد لتسويتك في أفعل التفضيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun them may refer to the most wretched group, since the person who directly killed the camel is most clearly and intensely wretched.
rows.anchor: والضمير في { لَهُمْ } يجوز أن يكون للأشقين والتفضيل في الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqat Allah is an accusative warning, meaning leave the camel alone or beware harming her; do not withhold or monopolize her drinking share.
rows.anchor: و { نَاقَةَ الله } نصب على التحذير ،   كقولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the warning that punishment would descend if they acted, then hamstrung the she-camel.
rows.anchor: فيما حذرهم منه من نزول العذاب إن فعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Damdama means to unleash punishment, related to the expression for a camel coated with fat.
rows.anchor: فأطلق عليهم العذاب ،   وهو من تكرير قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fate gives a grave warning about sin and calls every sinner to take heed.
rows.anchor: بسبب ذنبهم .   وفيه إنذار عظيم بعاقبه الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final pronoun refers to the punishment: it leveled them all, sparing neither young nor old.
rows.anchor: { فَسَوَّاهَا } الضمير للدمدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aftermath means consequences and retribution; a ruler imposing punishment normally fears repercussions and therefore shows restraint.
rows.anchor: أي : عاقبتها وتبعتها ؛ كما يخاف كل معاقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to Thamud: God leveled them or destroyed them and feared no consequence.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير لثمود على معنى : فسواها بالأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinan and Syrian codices read fa-la yakhafu; the Prophet's reading has lam yakhaf.
rows.anchor: وفي مصاحف أهل المدينة والشأم : فلا يخاف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that whoever recites Surat al-Shams is as though giving charity on everything illuminated by sun and moon.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الشمس ،   فكأنما تصدّق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma khalaqa can describe the All-Powerful who created male and female from one fluid; another view identifies them as Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: والقادر العظيم القدرة الذي قدر على خلق الذكر والأنثى من ماء واحد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's reading is wa-al-dhakari wa-al-untha.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : «والذكر والأنثى »

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads wa-alladhi khalaqa al-dhakara wa-al-untha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «والذي خلق الذكر والأنثى »

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads the nouns in the genitive as an apposition to the relative clause's position, meaning God's created male and female; God's name is omitted because He alone creates.
rows.anchor: وعن الكسائي : «وما خلق الذكر والأنثى بالجرّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All living creatures are either male or female; an intersex person's sex is known to God even if people find it ambiguous.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنّ الله لم يخلق خلقاً من ذوي الأرواح ليس بذكر ولا أنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who swore he had not seen any male or female that day breaks the oath if he saw an ambiguous intersex person, since that person is in reality one or the other.
rows.anchor: فلو حلف بالطلاق أنه لم يلق يومه ذكراً ولا أنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance to the truth is God's responsibility through establishing proofs and explaining the revealed laws.
rows.anchor: إن الإرشاد إلى الحق واجب علينا بنصب الدلائل وبيان الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guided person receives the reward of both abodes, as in the cited example.
rows.anchor: ثواب الدّارين للمهتدي ،   كقوله : { وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lifting the burden can mean forgiving him, teaching him the laws, or clearing his case after he proclaimed the message and it reached others.
rows.anchor: ووضعه عنه : أن غفر له ،   أو علم الشرائع

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reads the verb as halallna, meaning We unburdened or released.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أنس : «وحللنا » حططنا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads, We unburdened you of your burden.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «وحللنا عنك وقرك »

none: Only the verse text is provided.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Muhammad's mention by pairing it with His in the testimony of faith, calls to prayer, prayer formulas, sermons, Qur'anic verses, his titles, earlier scriptures, and the covenant requiring prophets and their peoples to believe in him.
rows.anchor: أن قرن بذكر الله في كلمة الشهادة والأذان والإقامة والتشهد والخطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added laka creates a suspenseful allusion then clarification: first what was expanded is left implicit before the breast is named, and similarly with your mention and burden.
rows.anchor: في زيادة لك ما في طريقة الإبهام والإيضاح ،   كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tur is annexed to Sinin, which denotes the region; Sinin can decline with waw and ya, retain ya, and take case endings on its nun.
rows.anchor: وأضيف الطور : وهو الجبل ،   إلى سنين : وهي البقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca, which protects those who enter it like a trustworthy keeper; amin can also mean protected from danger, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: والبلد : مكة حماها الله .   والأمين : من أمن الرجل أمانة فهو أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin may mean keeper, aman as a noun like karam, or passive: a place made safe from dangers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أمان ،   كما قيل : كرّام في كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath marks the honor of blessed places and the good from prophets and righteous people dwelling there: the fig and olive region is associated with Abraham's migration and Jesus' birth and upbringing; Sinai is where Moses was called; Mecca holds the Kaaba and Muhammad's birth and mission.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القسم بهذه الأشياء : الإبانة عن شرف البقاع المباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts to humanity: after the evidence, what makes you deny Judgment? Anyone denying truth is a liar, and human development from a drop through maturity and decline proves the Creator can resurrect.
rows.anchor: هو خطاب للإنسان على طريقة الالتفات ،   أي : فما يجعلك كاذباً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the address as directed to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse threatens unbelievers that God will judge them according to what they deserve.
rows.anchor: وعيد للكفار ،   وأنه يحكم عليهم بما هم أهله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When reciting this surah, the Prophet would answer that he was indeed a witness to it.
rows.anchor: أنه كان إذا قرأها قال : « بلى وأنا على ذلك من الشاهدين »

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises health and certainty through life and reward after death according to the number of people who recite the surah.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة التين أعطاه الله خصلتين : العافية واليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are singled out among created things because revelation is addressed to them and they are earth's noblest creatures.
rows.anchor: تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the vague Creator is specified as the one who made humanity to magnify the wonder of human formation.
rows.anchor: فقيل : { الذي خَلَقَ } مبهماً ،   ثم فسره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural clots means humanity generically, as in the cited verse, though an individual was created from one clot.
rows.anchor: لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع ،   كقوله : { إِنَّ الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Most Generous has unmatched generosity: He gives countless blessings, patiently delays punishment despite denial and disobedience, accepts repentance, and forgives grave sins; teaching knowledge through the pen is the highest such generosity.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال في زيادة كرمه على كل كرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾahu means he saw himself, with saw and knew among heart verbs taking two pronouns; it means knowing rather than sight because sight would not take both pronouns.
rows.anchor: أن رأى نفسه .   يقال : في أفعال القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaghna is the second object of the verb.
rows.anchor: و{ استغنى } هو المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address turns to the human as a warning against tyranny; al-rajʿa is a verbal noun meaning return, like bushra.
rows.anchor: واقع على طريقة الالتفات إلى الإنسان ،   تهديداً له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajʿa is a verbal noun meaning return, formed like bushra.
rows.anchor: والرجعى : مصدر كالبشرى بمعنى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: tell me about the person who stops a servant of God from praying.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: tell me about the person who stops a servant of God from praying.
rows.anchor: ومعناه : أخبرني عمن ينهى بعض عباد الله عن صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional asks whether the person who forbids worship of God himself is following a sound path in that prohibition.
rows.anchor: إن كان ذلك الناهي على طريقة سديدة فيما ينهى عنه من عبادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Or suppose he commands what he believes is good and piety, namely worship of idols.
rows.anchor: أو كان آمراً بالمعروف والتقوى فيما يأمر به من عبادة الأوثان كما يعتقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative condition asks what if he denies the truth and turns from true religion, leading into the reminder that God sees.
rows.anchor: وكذلك إن كان على التكذيب للحق والتولي عن الدين الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees a person's guidance or error and will recompense him accordingly; this is a threat.
rows.anchor: ويطلع على أحواله من هداه وضلاله فيجازيه على حسب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of arayta are the one who forbids and the conditional clause together.
rows.anchor: الذي ينهى مع الجملة الشرطية ،   وهما في موضع المفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first conditional's answer is omitted: if he is guided or commands piety, does he not know God sees? The answer is supplied by the second condition.
rows.anchor: هو محذوف ،   تقديره : إن كان على الهدى أو أمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question can validly serve as the answer to a condition, as the examples demonstrate.
rows.anchor: كما صحّ في قولك : إن أكرمتك أتكرمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second arayta between the objects repeats the expression for emphasis.
rows.anchor: هي زائدة مكرّرة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the person as Umayya ibn Khalaf, who stopped Salman from praying.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه أمية بن خلف كان ينهى سلمان عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl for forbidding worship and commanding worship of al-Lat; if he persists, God will seize his forelock and drag him to Hell.
rows.anchor: ردع لأبي جهل وخسوء له عن نهيه عن عبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means grasping and pulling something forcefully.
rows.anchor: والسفع : القبض على الشيء وجذبه بشدّة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معديكرب
rows.claim: A line by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdikarib supplies the word safiʿ in its sense of one who seizes.
rows.anchor:
قال عمرو بن معديكرب :
قَوْمٌ إذَا يَقَعُ الصَّرِيخُ رَأَيْتَهُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is read with a doubled n or by Ibn Masʿud as la-asfaʿa; the written alif marks pause, and the definite forelock relies on a known referent instead of possessive annexation.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «لنسفعنّ » بالنون المشدّدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasiyaa is apposition to the definite forelock; a descriptive indefinite phrase can have enough independent meaning to serve as its appositive.
rows.anchor: بدل من الناصية ؛ وجاز بدلها عن المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nominative or accusative readings also work as an insult, either as an implied sentence or direct insult.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «ناصية » على : هي ناصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful is a figurative attribution to its owner and is more vivid than directly describing him.
rows.anchor: ووصفها بالكذب والخطإ على الإسناد المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadi means a meeting place, while the intended meaning is the people who gather there.
rows.anchor: والنادي : المجلس الذي ينتدى فيه القوم

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's line about a council of red-haired men illustrates the gathering-place sense.
rows.anchor:
كما قال جرير :
لَهُمْ مَجْلِسٌ صُهْبُ السِّبَالِ أَذِلَّةٌ ***

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's line illustrates that maqamat means gathering places.
rows.anchor:
وقال زهير :
وَفِيهِمْ مَقَامَاتٌ حِسَانٌ وُجُوهُهُمْ ***

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet during prayer and boasted he had the largest gathering in the valley; the verses followed.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبا جهل مرّ برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads the verb in the passive: the punishment angels will be summoned.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : «سيدعى الزبانية »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, zabaniya means guards or police, from pushing; its singular form and variant derivations are explained lexically.
rows.anchor: والزبانية في كلام العرب : الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended referents are the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: والمراد : ملائكة العذاب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that had Abu Jahl summoned his gathering, the angels would have seized him before his eyes.
rows.anchor: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalla rebukes Abu Jahl; do not obey him but persist in what you are doing, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع لأبي جهل { لاَ تُطِعْهُ } أي اثبت على ما أنت عليه من عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration means continuing to pray, and drawing near means approaching one's Lord.
rows.anchor: { واسجد } ودم على سجودك ،   يريد : الصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says the servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
rows.anchor: أقرب ما يكون العبد إلى ربه إذا سجد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of reciting the whole Mufassal section to the one who recites Surat al-ʿAlaq.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصّل كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee has not reached the full extent of the Night of Decree's merit or the height of its rank.
rows.anchor: ولم تبلغ درايتك غاية فضلها ومنتهى علو قدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night exceeds a thousand months because of its religious benefits, including angels' descent and the decree of every wise matter.
rows.anchor: وسبب ارتقاء فضلها إلى هذه الغاية ما يوجد فيها من المصالح الدينية التي ذكرها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet mentioned an Israelite who bore arms fighting for God for a thousand months; believers envied him and felt their deeds too small, so they were given a night better than that span.
rows.anchor: رجلاً من بني إسرائيل لبس السلاح في سبيل الله ألف شهر ،   فعجب المؤمنون من ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says people formerly were called worshippers only after worshipping a thousand months; believers who revive this night merit the name even more.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنّ الرجل فيما مضى ما كان يقال له عابد حتى يعبد الله ألف شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels descend either to the lowest heaven or to earth.
rows.anchor: إلى السماء الدنيا ،   وقيل : إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, or a class of angels whom other angels see only on this night.
rows.anchor: جبريل .   وقيل : خلق من الملائكة لا تراهم الملائكة إلاّ تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They descend because of all matters God decreed for that year until the next.
rows.anchor: أي : تتنزل من أجل كل أمر قضاه الله لتلك السنة إلى قابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says min kulli imriʾ, for every person.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «من كل امرىء » أي : من أجل كل إنسان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the angels greet every believing man and woman that night.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لا يلقون مؤمناً ولا مؤمنة إلاّ سلموا عليه في تلك الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the night brings only safety and good, while other nights may bring either affliction or safety.
rows.anchor: ما هي إلاّ سلامة ،   أي : لا يقدر الله فيها إلاّ السلامة والخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a night of peace because the angels greet believers so abundantly.
rows.anchor: ما هي إلاّ سلام لكثرة ما يسلمون على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matlaʿ is read with the lām either open or kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «مطلع » بفتح اللام وكسرها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises the reward of fasting Ramadan and reviving the Night of Decree to a reciter of the surah.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة القدر أعطي من الأجر كمن صام رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rasul is an appositive to the clear proof; in ʿAbd Allah's reading it is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of that proof.
rows.anchor: و { رَّسُولٌ } بدل من البينة .   وفي قراءة عبد الله : «رسولا »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhuf means sheets or pages.
rows.anchor: { صُحُفاً } قراطيس { مُّطَهَّرَةً } من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purified means free of falsehood.
rows.anchor: { مُّطَهَّرَةً } من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writings are upright and speak with truth and justice.
rows.anchor: { فِيهَا كُتُبٌ } مكتوبات { قَيِّمَةٌ } مستقيمة ناطقة بالحق والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dispersal means turning away from truth, or splitting into factions: some believed, some denied, and some recognized it but stubbornly resisted.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتفرقهم : تفرقهم عن الحق وانقشاعهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are singled out after the two groups are paired because they knew the clear proof from their own scriptures; abandoning it makes their division worse than that of pagans without scripture.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا على علم به لوجوده في كتبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah and Gospel commanded only the hanif religion, but their followers altered and substituted it.
rows.anchor: يعني في التوراة والإنجيل إلاّ بالدين الحنيفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Din al-qayyima means the religion of the upright community; another reading supplies din and takes qayyima as describing the community.
rows.anchor: أي : دين الملة القيمة .   وقرىء ؛ «وذلك الدين القيمة »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were commanded by the scriptures for the purpose of worshipping God in this manner.
rows.anchor: معناه : وما أمروا بما في الكتابين إلاّ لأجل أن يعبدوا الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads illa an yaʿbudu, meaning that they should worship.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «إلا أن يعبدوا »

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ reads al-bariʾa with hamza; other readers use the conventional light form, as in nabi, abandoning the original hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع : «البريئة » بالهمز ؛ والقرّاء على التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is khiyar al-bariyya, the plural of khayr, by analogy with the plurals jiyad and tibab.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «خيار البرية » جمع خير

none: Only the verse text is provided.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athqal is the plural of thiql, meaning household goods or baggage.
rows.anchor: الأثقال : جمع ثقل .   وهو متاع البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden treasures inside the earth are called its burdens.
rows.anchor: جعل ما في جوفها من الدفائن أثقالاً لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the second blast, the violent quake makes the earth expel its contents and resurrect its dead; people ask in horror what is happening, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: زلزلت هذه الزلزلة الشديدة ولفظت ما في بطنها ؛ وذلك عند النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view assigns the question to unbelievers, since they denied resurrection; believers instead say this is what the Merciful promised and the messengers spoke truly.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هذا قول الكافر ؛ لأنه كان لا يؤمن بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's speaking can be a metaphor: God creates conditions that show the observers why it shook and expelled the dead and verify the prophets' warnings.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز عن إحداث الله تعالى فيها من الأحوال ما يقوم مقام التحديث باللسان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, God makes the earth speak literally about the good and evil done upon it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ينطقها الله على الحقيقة .   وتخبر بما عمل عليها من خير وشرّ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the earth will testify against every person about what they did on its surface.
rows.anchor: تشهد على كل أحد بما عمل على ظهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawmaʾidhin may be apposition to idha, with both governed by tuhaddith; alternatively idha has an implicit governor and yawmaʾidhin is governed by tuhaddith.
rows.anchor: { يَوْمَئِذٍ } بدل من ( إذا ) ،   وناصبهما { تُحَدِّثُ }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuhaddith has an omitted first object; akhbaraha is the second, with people as the understood audience, omitted to focus on the reports and magnify the day.
rows.anchor: قد حذف أولهما ،   والثاني : أخبارها ،   وأصله تحدث الخلق أخبارها
